Origin · Chapter I

Finca
El Paraiso

We import coffees from Finca El Paraiso directly — because we are their European partners. Direct trade means we know exactly who grew each bean, when it was harvested, and how it was processed.

This is a farm where fermentation is engineering, not guesswork. Every batch is measured, logged and reproduced with scientific precision.

Finca El Paraiso started as 2.5 hectares of unused land given to a management student named Diego Bermúdez in 2008. In 2015 it won its first regional competition. In 2018 a lot from El Paraiso fetched $54.10 per pound at Cup of Excellence Colombia — the highest price of the auction despite finishing 10th in the scoring. The market understood something exceptional was happening.

Together with his brother Alexander and cousin Cristian Zúñiga, Diego founded INDESTEC — a research company that applies biocatalysis, bioreactor-controlled fermentation, thermal shock, and ecological mechanical drying to every batch. Today the farm is led by Daniel and Alexander Bermúdez. The farm sits at 1,960 m.a.s.l. in the municipality of Piendamó, Cauca, on clay-loam soil rich in organic matter. 7,000 coffee trees on 1.7 hectares, farmed under semi-shade using biological and organic methods.

About Us

Caffeine Fellowship
